label: Tighten
instruction: Tighten slide {{SLIDE}}: at most five bullets, at most ten words each, and cut every word that is not carrying a fact. Keep the meaning and keep the numbers.

label: Make it a claim
instruction: Rewrite the title of slide {{SLIDE}} so it states the point instead of naming the topic — "Churn is a pricing problem", not "Churn analysis". Leave the bullets alone unless the new title makes one redundant.
help: Title states the point, not the topic

label: Speaker notes
instruction: Write the speaker notes for slide {{SLIDE}}. Say what the presenter SAYS, not what the slide shows: expand the bullets into spoken sentences, add the detail behind each claim, and end with the transition into the next slide. Never restate the bullets. Do not change the slide itself.
help: What you say, not what the slide shows

label: Make it visual
instruction: Slide {{SLIDE}} is text where it could be a picture. If one number carries the point, make it a bigFact slide with that number and a one-line label. If it compares two things, make it twoColumn with the compared items as the first entry of each column. If the user's Ledger has a collection that evidences it, make it a chart bound to that collection. Otherwise leave the layout alone and say why in your reply.
help: Re-flow into a bigFact, comparison or chart

label: Add evidence
instruction: Slide {{SLIDE}} asserts something without support. Add the number, date or source that backs it — but ONLY from the deck's own material or the user's Ledger collections listed in your context. If nothing supports it, say so in your reply and change nothing: an invented statistic is worse than a thin slide.
help: Back the claim — never invent one

label: Split
instruction: Slide {{SLIDE}} is carrying more than one idea. Split it into two slides in place, each with one claim as its title, and divide the existing bullets between them. Add nothing new.
